verses.145:4: Sairá o seu {spiritus}, e {terram}: * naquele dia perecerão todos os pensamentos deles.

verses.145:7a: {qui7} a verdade para sempre, † {judicium}: * dá alimento aos famintos.
verses.145:7b: O Senhor solta os acorrentados: * o Senhor ilumina os cegos.
verses.145:8b: O Senhor ergue os {elisos}, * o Senhor ama os justos.
verses.145:9: O Senhor guarda os {advenas}, † amparará o órfão e a viúva: * e {disperdet} os caminhos dos pecadores.

decisions.why: The soul addressed with the imperative, the vocative between verb and object. The finished psalms that open the same way — 102:1, 102:2, 102:22, 103:1, 103:35 *Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino* — all read *Bendize, ó minha alma, ao Senhor* (the ánima mea row): the Latin's order, *tu* to the soul, *ó* so that the vocative is heard with the imperative. The same build here. This colon is also the head of the Tuesday Lauds antiphon *Lauda ánima mea Dóminum, qui érigit elísos et díligit justos* ([Day3 Laudes2], Psalmi major) and of the Offertory of the 3rd Sunday after Easter and Ember Friday of Pentecost (Pasc3-0, Pasc7-5, grep): *Louva, ó minha alma, o Senhor* reads alone and runs on into *que ergue os derrubados e ama os justos*. MS1932 has these words; DRB 'Praise the Lord, O my soul' moves the vocative back.

options.label: Louva, ó minha alma, o Senhor

forms.lauda: Louva, ó minha alma, o Senhor

options.note: Ruling: 102:1 / 103:1's build, the Latin's order. MS1932 word for word.

options.label: Louva o Senhor, ó minha alma

forms.lauda: Louva o Senhor, ó minha alma

options.note: The plainer order (DRB, DM1962 'Louva o Senhor, minha alma'). Breaks the kinship with 102:1 / 103:1.

decisions.why: 103:33 has the same colon with *quámdiu sum* (*psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum*) and reads *entoarei salmos ao meu Deus, enquanto eu existir* (D39: *esse* absolute → *existir*). The future perfect here is the more natural source of the Portuguese future subjunctive, so identical Portuguese fits both Latin forms (rule 6). *Enquanto eu viver* (DM1962 'enquanto viver'; MS1932 paraphrases 'durante toda a minha vida') is plainer but names life, where the Latin says being and has just said *in vita mea*.

options.label: enquanto eu viver
options.note: DM1962's verb; plainer, but repeats 'vida' of the first colon in another word.

decisions.why: *Nolíte* + infinitive is the ordinary Latin prohibition; Portuguese says it with the negative subjunctive. *confídere in → confiar em* (row, working; 117:8 *É melhor confiar no Senhor, do que confiar no homem*); *príncipes* as 117:9 *do que esperar nos príncipes* and every other place of *princeps* in the finished psalms (concord.py). The plural address is *vós* (rule 3); *confieis* is safe under the homograph ban. Brazilian circulation checked (consult/lh-cnbb-salmo-145146.html, fetched): the CNBB Liturgia das Horas has 'Não ponhais vossa fé nos que mandam' — from the Hebrew (נְדִיבִים), and it drops the princes; not a witness of sense.

options.label: Não confieis
options.note: Ruling. DRB 'Put not your trust in'.

options.label: Não queirais confiar
options.note: The literal tier: keeps 'nolle' as a verb of will. In Portuguese it is heard as a softened request, which the Latin idiom is not.

options.label: Não ponhais a vossa confiança
options.note: Near DM1962 / CNBB 'Não ponhais (a) vossa fé'; longer, and loses the verb of the row.

decisions.why: The second colon stands in apposition to the first, with no conjunction (the Greek has καί, the Latin none). MS1932 supplies *nem*; DRB keeps the bare apposition ('in the children of men'). The bare form keeps the Latin's build — the princes *are* sons of men, which is the psalm's argument (145:4) — where *nem* makes two classes of people. *Filhos dos homens* as in every finished place (4:3, 11:2, 48:3, 113:24 …).

options.label: nos filhos dos homens
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's apposition. DRB.

options.label: nem nos filhos dos homens
options.note: MS1932; the Greek's καί. Makes a second class of people where the Latin gives a second name for the first.

decisions.why: Two senses are open in the Latin: no salvation can come from them, and there is no salvation in them for themselves (the next verse: they die). *Em quem não há salvação* keeps both, and it is DRB's 'in whom there is no salvation'. MS1932 'que não podem salvar' and DM1962 'que não pode salvar' choose the first. *salus → salvação* (D6); 3:3 *Non est salus ipsi* → *Não há salvação para ele*.

options.label: em quem não há salvação
options.note: Ruling: both senses kept.

options.label: que não podem salvar
options.note: MS1932. Plainer; closes the Latin's openness to one sense.

decisions.why: The breath that leaves a man at death (πνεῦμα). The glossary's *sopro* row (102:16) is for wind-and-breath at once and says 'not for spíritus of a person'; 103:29 *áuferes spíritum eórum* (the same death, the same image) reads *tirareis o espírito deles*, and 30:6 *o meu espírito*. So *espírito*, the Latin's word. *Sopro* is the image the Hebrew (רוּחוֹ) and the CNBB LH ('Ao faltar-lhe o respiro') have; the Latin's word is not narrower than that, but the Portuguese *espírito* is, so the option stays. *Sairá* as 103:23 *Exíbit homo* → *Sairá o homem*.

options.label: espírito
options.note: Ruling: = 103:29; the Latin's word. MS1932 'alma' (gloss), DRB 'spirit'.

options.label: sopro
options.note: The breath; closer to the physical image, further from the Latin word.

decisions.why: Two things are open. (1) The subject of *revertétur*: grammatically *spíritus*, in sense the man (the Hebrew: he returns to his ground); the Portuguese with the subject unexpressed carries the same openness. (2) *In terram suam* is the earth he was made of (Gn 3:19; 103:29 *in púlverem suum reverténtur* → *voltarão ao seu pó*). In Brazilian Portuguese *voltar à sua terra* is heard first as going home to one's native land. *Para a sua terra* has the same risk. MS1932 explains with 'ao seu pó', which is 103:29's different Latin word. Ruled for the Latin's word and the ear's risk put to the blind reader; if it hears the homeland, the verse gets *à terra de onde veio*-type help or the 103:29 wording.

options.label: voltará à sua terra
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's words. Risk: heard as 'go back home'. To be tested on the ambiguity reader.

options.label: voltará ao seu pó
options.note: MS1932; 103:29's wording. Right sense, another Latin word (púlvis).

options.label: tornará à sua terra
options.note: The same words with 'tornar', slightly more solemn; the homeland risk is the same.

decisions.latin: Beátus, cujus Deus Jacob adjútor ejus
decisions.why: *cujus … ejus* is the resumptive pronoun of the Hebrew relative; Portuguese says it once. The subject of *Beátus* is unnamed: *aquele* supplied (grammar, D2; DRB 'Blessed is he'). Built as 83:6 *Beátus vir, cujus est auxílium abs te* → *Bem-aventurado o homem cujo auxílio vem de vós*, and 32:12 / 143:15 *cujo Deus é o Senhor*. *adjútor → auxílio* (row, uniform; *auxiliador* refused for length and currency). *Deus de Jacó* as 45:8, 75:7, 83:9.

options.label: Bem-aventurado aquele cujo auxílio é o Deus de Jacó

forms.beatus: Bem-aventurado aquele cujo auxílio é o Deus de Jacó

options.note: Ruling. The Latin's order of the relative kept as far as Portuguese allows.

options.label: Bem-aventurado aquele que tem por auxílio o Deus de Jacó

forms.beatus: Bem-aventurado aquele que tem por auxílio o Deus de Jacó

options.note: DM1962's build ('Feliz o que tem por auxílio'). Supplies 'ter'; one syllable longer.

decisions.latin: spes ejus in Dómino, Deo ipsíus
decisions.why: No relative and no conjunction: *spes ejus* may continue the relative (DRB 'whose hope is in the Lord his God'; MS1932 'e cuja esperança está') or stand as a statement (his hope is in the Lord). The asyndeton with *a sua esperança está* keeps both readings, and the copula is supplied (D2). *Seu Deus* for *Deo ipsíus*; *ipsíus* adds only emphasis, which Portuguese does not need after *seu*. The relative *que fez o céu e a terra* then follows *seu Deus* directly, as the formula row asks (133:3, 120:2, 123:8).

options.label: a sua esperança está
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's asyndeton.

options.label: cuja esperança está
options.note: DRB's reading made explicit; closes the Latin to one parse.

options.label: e cuja esperança está
options.note: MS1932; supplies a conjunction too.

decisions.why: The relative continues the chain of 145:6 *qui fecit*: God who made, who keeps, does, gives. In Portuguese a prayed verse opening *Que guarda a verdade para sempre, † faz juízo…* reads as a headless relative subject of *faz* ('who keeps truth does justice'), or as an exclamation. The subject named and the verb made finite is grammar (D2), as Ps 134:7a–7b did (the Latinist passed it). *custodíre → guardar* (row); *in sǽculum → para sempre* (D23).

options.label: Ele guarda
options.note: Ruling: finite, subject named.

options.label: Que guarda
options.note: The relative kept, as the Latin's chain of 'qui'. Heard as an exclamation or a headless relative at the head of a verse.

options.label: Ele, que guarda
options.note: 134:21's 'ele que habita': both the pronoun and the relative. Makes 'faz' the main verb of 'ele'.

decisions.why: 102:6 *et judícium ómnibus injúriam patiéntibus* reads *e juízo para todos os que sofrem injustiça*, and the *injúriam pati* row says 145:7 should copy it (*injúria* in Brazil is an insult; ἀδικούμενοι). *fácere judícium* is an open row: bare *fazer juízo* is heard as forming an opinion (118:121), but with *para* and a class of people it can only be judgement given in their favour. *Faz justiça aos* (MS1932; CNBB 'faz justiça aos que são oprimidos') is the idiom, but *justiça* is *justítia*'s, and *justiça … injustiça* would chime.

options.label: faz juízo para os que sofrem injustiça

forms.judicium: faz juízo para os que sofrem injustiça

options.note: Ruling: 102:6's wording.

options.label: faz justiça aos que sofrem injustiça

forms.judicium: faz justiça aos que sofrem injustiça

options.note: The Portuguese idiom (MS1932 'faz justiça aos que sofrem injúria'); spends 'justiça', and chimes.

options.label: faz juízo aos que sofrem injustiça

forms.judicium: faz juízo aos que sofrem injustiça

options.note: The dative kept with 'a'; 'fazer juízo a' is not idiomatic.

decisions.why: *elídere* is to dash down, strike out, crush (L&S); the Greek κατερραγμένους, those dashed to the ground. *érigere → erguer* (112:7 *érigens páuperem → ergue o pobre*). *Derrubados* keeps the blow and the fall, and pairs with *ergue*. *Abatidos* is the familiar pair ('ergue os abatidos') but in Brazil is heard first as downcast in spirit; *caídos* (MS1932; the CNBB LH 'o caído') loses the violence and is the Latin *cadere*, which 144:14 sets beside this very word (*Allevat Dóminus omnes qui córruunt: et érigit omnes elísos* — Ps 144 is being translated in parallel; the two should agree). The verse is sung in the Tuesday Lauds antiphon (*Lauda ánima mea Dóminum, qui érigit elísos et díligit justos*), so *que ergue os derrubados e ama os justos* must read well after *Louva, ó minha alma, o Senhor*.

options.label: derrubados
options.note: Ruling: struck down; the image of the blow.

options.label: abatidos
options.note: Familiar; heard first as dejected.

options.label: caídos
options.note: MS1932; plain, but it is 144:14's 'qui córruunt', a different verb.

options.label: esmagados
options.note: L&S 'crush'; one does not 'raise' what is crushed.

decisions.why: *ádvena → forasteiro* (D39, from 38:13b; 93:6 *Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt → Assassinaram a viúva e o forasteiro*, the same triad of widow, stranger and orphan). Here the Greek is προσηλύτους, as — by the look of the triad — in 93:6; D39 joined *ádvena* to *íncola* on πάροικος at 38:13b; the Portuguese word serves both. *Estrangeiro* (CNBB LH, DM1962) names a nationality; *peregrinos* (MS1932) is *peregrínus*'s own word.

options.label: forasteiros
options.note: Ruling: the row (D39); = 93:6.

options.label: estrangeiros
options.note: DM1962 and CNBB LH ('o estrangeiro'); the Hebrew family's word; aliénus has 'estranho'.

options.label: peregrinos
options.note: MS1932; the row keeps it for peregrínus.

decisions.why: *dispérdere → exterminar* (row, working; kept apart from *dispérgere*, *períre*, *disperíre*), already with a non-personal object at 11:4 (*os lábios enganadores*). *Exterminar os caminhos* is a strong collocation, but the Latin's verb is strong too, and the Greek ἀφανιεῖ ('make vanish') is its own reading. *Destruirá* (MS1932 'destruirá os caminhos'; DRB 'destroy') is plainer and is the option. The Latin's order (object before verb) is changed to the Portuguese order; the future kept, as *suscípiet* (*amparará*) beside the present *custódit*.

options.label: exterminará
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: destruirá
options.note: MS1932, DRB. Plainer with 'caminhos'; the verb is 'destrúere' elsewhere.

options.label: fará desaparecer
options.note: The Greek ἀφανιεῖ; longer, and not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: The apposition *Deus tuus* after *Dóminus*, then the vocative. The finished psalms leave the vocative of the city bare (121:2 *nos teus átrios, Jerusalém*; 136:5 *Se eu me esquecer de ti, Jerusalém*). In the Latin's order the mediant falls on *Sião* and the final on *geração*: an accidental -ão / -ão rhyme at mediant and final (checks.py), which the Latin (*Sion / generatiónem*) does not really have. The vocative is moved before the apposition (order, D2), so the mediant falls on *Deus*; DM1962 also ends a colon on *o teu Deus*. *Pelos séculos* for *in sǽcula* alone (row, settled D43, which names 145:10); *de geração em geração* (formula row, which names 145:10).

options.label: Sião, o teu Deus
options.note: Ruling: the rhyme avoided by order alone.

options.label: o teu Deus, Sião
options.note: The Latin's order; rhymes Sião / geração at mediant and final.

options.label: o teu Deus, ó Sião
options.note: MS1932 'ó Sião'; the same rhyme.

choices.145:2a: The Alleluia title (LXX αλληλουια Αγγαιου καὶ Ζαχαριου; MS1932 'Aleluia: De Ageu e de Zacarias'; DRB 'Alleluia, of Aggeus and Zacharias') is not in DO's Latin, which opens on 'Lauda, ánima mea'; as in Pss 110–113 and 134–135 it is not reproduced (D7). 'na minha vida' for 'in vita mea' as 62:5, 103:33; the antiphon 'Laudábo * Deum meum in vita mea' ([Day3 Laudes1], [Daya6 Vespera], monastic Saturday Vespers) will read 'Louvarei o meu Deus na minha vida'. 'Senhor … Senhor' at the flex and mediant is the Latin's Dóminum / Dóminum. The Offertory (Pasc3-0, Pasc7-5) has 'quámdiu ero'; the Portuguese is the same.
choices.145:4: 'ejus' (singular) against 'eórum' (plural) kept: 'o seu espírito' / 'os pensamentos deles'. cogitátio → pensamento (row); 55:6 'todos os seus pensamentos'. períre → perecer (row). 'in illa die' → 'naquele dia'.
choices.145:5: The formula 'que fez o céu e a terra' (row) follows 'seu Deus' directly; 'tudo o que neles há' as 95:11 'et ómnia quæ in eis sunt'. 145:6 is carried inside the DO verse 145:5; the inline (6) marker is not reproduced.
choices.145:7a: esca → alimento where God gives food (110:4, 135:25, 103:27); esuriéntes → famintos (106:5, 106:36).
choices.145:7b: The row 'compedíti · sólvere' names this verse: 'solta os acorrentados', = 101:21. illumináre → iluminar (18:9 'ilumina os olhos'); the Latin says the Lord gives light to the blind, not that he opens their eyes (the Hebrew, DM1962 and the CNBB LH 'abre os olhos aos cegos'). The fourfold anaphora 'O Senhor' of 7b–9 is kept.
choices.145:9: suscípere (persons) → amparar (D19), the Latin future kept ('amparará') beside the present 'guarda'; pupíllus → órfão (row); the Latin order 'o órfão e a viúva' kept (the CNBB LH inverts it). via → caminho; 1:1 'no caminho dos pecadores'.
choices.145:10: 'O Senhor reinará' puts the subject first where the Latin has the verb first (natural order; 9:37 'O Senhor reinará para sempre'). The vocative is placed before the apposition to avoid the Sião / geração rhyme (decision sion).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps145.md (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Precedents from the finished psalms by ps145/concord.py (adapted from ps144/concord.py): 102:1 / 103:1 (the soul addressed), 103:33 (psallam Deo meo quámdiu sum), 117:8–9 (confiar em; príncipes), 103:23 / 103:29 (Exíbit; spíritum; reverténtur), 83:6 (Beátus … cujus auxílium), 102:6 (injúriam patiéntibus), 101:21 (compedítos, sólvere), 112:7 (érigere), 93:6 (widow, stranger, orphan), 121:2 / 136:5 (bare vocative of the city). Liturgical uses by grep of content/do Latin: the antiphons 'Laudábo Deum meum in vita mea' (Psalmi major [Day3 Laudes1], [Daya6 Vespera], monastic feria 7 Vespers) and 'Lauda ánima mea Dóminum, qui érigit elísos et díligit justos' ([Day3 Laudes2]); the Offertory 'Lauda, ánima mea, Dóminum … quámdiu ero, allelúja' (Pasc3-0, Pasc7-5). 'Nolíte confídere' occurs nowhere else in the psalter or the DO Latin liturgy except Jer 7:4 (another text). Brazilian circulation: the CNBB Liturgia das Horas Sl 145(146) fetched (consult/lh-cnbb-salmo-145146.html; see circulation.md); the Lectionary refrains 'Bendize, ó minha alma, ao Senhor' and 'Felizes os pobres em espírito' reported by a web search summary only, unverified. Hard readings: 145:4 in terram suam (homeland risk), 145:5 the resumptive cujus … ejus and the asyndeton of spes ejus, 145:7a the relative chain, 145:8b elísos.

Hard checks pass. Rhyme Sião / geração at mediant and final in 145:10 (Latin order) — fixed by order (decision sion). Soft length flags accepted: 145:2a final +6 (= 103:33 word for word; D25's two words for psállere); 145:2b first -4 (nolíte + infinitive is one Portuguese verb); 145:5 first +6 (D19's six-syllable bem-aventurado and the supplied aquele); 145:9 final +5 (exterminará; destruirá is the option, one syllable less); 145:10 final -6 (the formula de geração em geração).
